note: Lean states the bounds as strip bounds with a loss of width (`surfHeight 2 σ`, `surfHeight 3 σ`) and takes `C`, `D`, `E` as abstract inputs, whereas [M] speaks of dual block norms on a fixed smaller strip. The constants `C/6` and `(D+3C²E)/24` are the same.

lemma pennies {Φ : Bridge G P} {U : TextS 3 P G} {T : TextS 4 P G} (V : SeaFoam P G) {σ C D E} (h : Fresh (celestial Φ) σ) (hs : 0<σ) (hx : Pungent U σ) (hy : Pungent T σ) (hp : Laureate U Φ σ C) (hq : Laureate T Φ σ D) (he : Poster σ V) (hb : Freezer (slabW G P.L|>.dual) (slabW G P.L) V σ E) (hE : 0≤E) :
    (∀ i j,Firm (surfHeight 2 σ) (C/6) (pureStroke Φ U i j)) ∧ (∀ i j,Firm (surfHeight 3 σ) ((D+3*(C*(E*C)))/24) (pressStroke Φ U T V i j)) := by

proof_context.conclusion: `pennies`: the cubic kernel `pureStroke` has strip bound `C/6` and the quartic kernel `pressStroke` has strip bound `(D + 3*(C*(E*C)))/24`, where `C, D` bound the cubic and quartic vertices (`Laureate`) and `E` the inverse (`Poster`).

  have he : merit S t p R ∘ viewS U=ᶠ[𝓝 0] victory F t p R ρ := salary h hS t hp K
  rw [← (he.iteratedFDeriv ℝ 3).eq_of_nhds,
      ← verge h hS t hk, ← verge h hS t hk, ← verge h hS t hk]
  exact (mural h hp hS t K).accrue ..

proof_context.conclusion: The third derivative of the stationary action equals that of the fine action on the lifted legs.
